question.text: A short straight object of height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> lies before the central axis of a spherical mirror whose focal length has absolute value <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced close="|" open="|"><mi>f</mi></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. The image of object produced by the mirror is of height <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and has the same orientation of the object. One may conclude from the information:

options.text: Image is real, same side of convex mirror.
Image is virtual, opposite side of concave mirror.
Image is real, same side of concave mirror.
Image is virtual, opposite side of convex mirror.

solution.text: Since orientation is same image is virtual. Since image is smaller the mirror has to be convex
